findings.title: Pause menu item will never render in list view because rulerRule is undefined
findings.body: The condition `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` will always be false when `rulerRule` is undefined, which is the case when AlertRuleMenu is used from the alert list view (the primary motivation of this PR). Even though `canPause` may be true via the grafana prom rule abilities path, the menu item is gated on `rulerRule` being a valid Grafana ruler rule. Users will see no Pause option in the list view despite having permission.

findings.title: Delete menu item will never render in list view because rulerRule is undefined
findings.body: The condition `canDelete && rulerRule` requires `rulerRule` to be truthy. In the list view (the primary use case this PR targets), `rulerRule` is undefined, so the Delete menu item will never appear even when the user has delete permissions via the grafana prom rule abilities. The `handleDelete` callback also expects a `RulerRuleDTO` argument, so this needs a redesign to work without ruler data.

findings.title: Silence drawer will never open from list view because ruler rule type check fails
findings.body: The condition `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` on line 104 will be false when `rule` is undefined (which is the case in the list view where only `promRule` is provided). The user can click 'Silence notifications' in the dropdown menu (since `canSilence` can be true via grafana abilities), which sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true, but the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` component will never render because the guard condition fails. The user experiences a non-functional menu item.

findings.title: Federated rule check hardcoded to false is a regression for Mimir/Loki federated groups
findings.body: The previous implementation checked `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` which inspected `source_tenants` on the rule group. The new code hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO comment. This means federated Mimir/Loki rules will now incorrectly show Edit, Delete, Pause, and Duplicate actions that should be disabled for federated rules. The `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` type passed to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` does not carry the `source_tenants` information needed to make this determination.

findings.title: Extra closing brace in Grafana rule key generation
findings.body: The template literal `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}}` has a trailing extra `}` character. While this won't cause a functional failure (it's just a React key), it produces inconsistent key values and may cause confusion during debugging. Should be `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}`.

findings.title: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities invokes sub-hooks with API calls even when skipToken is passed
findings.body: When `skipToken` is passed to `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (e.g., for non-Grafana rules in AlertRuleMenu), the hook still calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` which unconditionally invokes `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` (making an RTK Query call to get alertmanager configuration status) and `useCanSilenceInFolder(undefined)`. Since React hooks cannot be conditionally called, every non-Grafana rule in the list view triggers these unnecessary API calls and hook invocations, potentially causing performance degradation on pages with many data-source-managed rules.

findings.title: Redundant type narrowing makes promAlertingRule always equal to rule
findings.body: Inside the `if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule))` block, the expression `rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined` is redundant because the outer condition already guarantees `rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting` and `rule` is truthy. `promAlertingRule` will always equal `rule`. While not a runtime bug, it obscures intent and the `undefined` branch is dead code.
